cands.bio: Republican and first-time candidate for Alabama State Senate District 22. Farmer, Army veteran and small business owner from Robertsdale. He helped build a family nursery business. He defeated incumbent Sen. Greg Albritton in the May 2026 Republican primary.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or the year he came to or lived in Alabama beyond the 'lifelong resident' claim. We found no record of prior elected office, legislative work or a policy career. We found no statements on data centers, development or growth limits, restrictions on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, school choice or teacher pay. His campaign site names no specific policies on homestead property taxes, guns beyond a general pledge, or police pay. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. No news coverage of controversies or foreign ties was found.

qual.background: Farmer and co-builder of a multi-generation family nursery business who is a small business owner; served in the U.S. Army on active duty and in the Guard. He has held no prior elected office, according to the campaign site, which calls him a first-time candidate.
qual.why: Business ownership and management fits the middle band. He has no legislative, policy or budget career on record.
qual.label: Business ownership and management fits the middle band. He has no legislative, policy or budget career on record.

second-amendment.evidence: Says law-abiding Alabamians' Second Amendment rights should not be taken away or chipped at piece by piece. The campaign site gives no specific policy on red-flag laws, suppressors or purchase ages.

pro-life.evidence: Says life begins at conception and that he won't apologize for protecting life, including in cases of rape and incest. He was glad to see Roe v. Wade overturned.

workers-first.evidence: Says he will stand firm behind President Trump and ICE in enforcing the law and securing the border. The page says nothing on H-1B visas.

back-police-order.evidence: Pledges to stand up for law enforcement, firefighters and other first responders and veterans in Montgomery. He names no specific pay or pension proposals.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Pledges to cut taxes and wasteful spending. He does not mention property or homestead taxes specifically.

cands.bio: Democratic nominee for Alabama State Senate District 22 in 2026. Born in Baldwin County. Has worked in restaurants, as an ESL missionary teacher in Texas, as an assisted-living caregiver, and as a Baldwin County Sheriff's Office corrections officer. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from Tabitha's List (Sway voting group by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot (Sway voting group by Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We found no record of Ashley Sharpe holding elected office, so there are no legislative actions to report. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We could not find where she grew up, when she lived in Alabama as an adult, or when or whether she moved here. We found no stated positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, immigration or H-1B visas, gun laws, school choice or vouchers, or police pay and pensions. We also found no dated statements on data centers or development. Her campaign site mentions overdevelopment only in passing.
